record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Variance and CLT for fringe-clade counts
record.original_question: Fix a finite clade shape χ in DTCS(n), and let N_n(χ) be the number of copies of χ appearing as fringe clades in the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree. Prove that n^{-1} Var(N_n(χ)) converges to a finite limit σ^2(χ), and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for N_n(χ).

evidence.quote: In particular, the number Nn(χ) of copies of a size-i clade χ in DTCS(n) will satisfy n−1E[Nn(χ)] → p(χ)/i.
Open Problem 5 Prove that n−1var(Nn(χ)) converges to some limit σ2(χ) and that the corresponding CLT holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n) on $n\ge 2$ leaves, defined recursively as follows: starting from the root clade of size $n$, a clade of size $m\ge 2$ is split into two child clades of sizes $i$ and $m-i$ (with $1\le i\le m-1$) with probability
$$q(m,i)=\frac{1}{h_{m-1}}\cdot\frac{1}{i}\cdot\frac{m-i+i}{?}\quad\text{i.e.}\quad q(m,i)=\frac{m}{2h_{m-1}}\cdot\frac{1}{i(m-i)},$$
where $h_{m-1}=\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}1/j$, and the split is performed independently across clades until every clade has size 1 (a leaf). The resulting object is a rooted binary tree with $n$ labelled (or unlabelled) leaves.

A finite clade shape $\chi$ of size $i$ is an isomorphism class of such a tree on $i$ leaves. For each internal node $v$ of DTCS(n), the subtree rooted at $v$ (a "fringe clade") has some shape; let $N_n(\chi)$ denote the number of internal nodes of DTCS(n) whose fringe clade has shape $\chi$. It is known that there exists a constant $p(\chi)>0$ such that
$$n^{-1}\mathbb{E}[N_n(\chi)]\to p(\chi)/i\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.$$

Prove the following two assertions:
(a) The limit $\sigma^2(\chi):=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\mathrm{Var}(N_n(\chi))$ exists and is finite.
(b) The central limit theorem holds: as $n\to\infty$,
$$\frac{N_n(\chi)-\mathbb{E}[N_n(\chi)]}{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(N_n(\chi))}}\;\xrightarrow{d}\;\mathcal{N}(0,1).$$
artifact.category_tag: Random trees and central limit theorems
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint on the harmonic descent chain and applications to critical beta-splitting trees explicitly states that it answers Open Problems 5 and 6, establishing a CLT for the fringe-clade counts $N_n(\chi)$ (with appropriate centering and variance scaling) for every finite clade shape $\chi$. Thus the problem appears solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics for the harmonic descent chain and applications to critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: we answer Open Problems 5 and 6 ... deducing central limit theorems for various statistics of the tree. For any k, [N_n(k)-E[N_n(k)]]/sqrt(Var(N_n(k))) →d N(0,1). A central limit theorem also holds for N_n(χ) for all χ of size |χ|∈ℕ.
status_evidence.claim: The paper resolves Open Problem 5, proving variance scaling and a CLT for fringe clade counts N_n(χ).
